![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224989/assets/ca003331d04113119019996f15296ec2ab16fa0c14227a12f5f421c4c4103746.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224989/assets/f0c1c9df42fc2ed772353baec0f81e796485d8bf3c1cd9dde234e74e39a04c56.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{2}{9}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{7}{9}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}$

Knowing that $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3})}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3})}=\frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{2}}.
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{7\cdot 2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{14}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
